newsitem.title: UK: IFC emerging market index rises 0.4 pct to 294.14.
newsitem.headline: IFC emerging market index rises 0.4 pct to 294.14.

text.p: The International Finance Corporation's benchmark composite index of emerging market equities IFC/IPRD, denominated in dollars, rose 0.4 percent to 294.14 at the start of play on Friday.
Latin America was up 0.4 percent day-on-day to 532.54, Asia was up 0.5 percent at 249.46, and Europe, Middle East and Africa were up 0.2 percent at 138.54.
The IFC index touched a 1996 high of 308.77 on July 4, up from the year's 275.79 low, recorded on January 1.
ING Barings' Global Emerging Market Index BFFO, also denominated in dollars, was up 0.30 percent day-on-day at 159.35 at 1020 GMT.
The year's high was 165.948, reached on July 3. It touched the year's 148.85 low on January 2.
Morgan Stanley's dollar-denominated Emerging Markets Free index .CEMF=USD, was up 0.30 percent at 476.377, calculated after the close of play on Thursday.
It touched a 1996 high at 505.452 on July 4; the year's 458.369 low was recorded on January 1.

All indices are capitalisation-weighted and are calculated daily. The IFC index measures returns on equities, liquid and accessible to foreign investors, from 26 emerging market countries. It is updated at 2300 GMT.
The BEMI index measures equity returns from some 20 emerging market countries, with the latest changes reported by 0900 GMT.
The MSCI Free measures equity returns from 22 emerging market nations. Changes are reported with one day's lag at 1300 GMT.
The J.P. Morgan emerging market local currency index ELMI, its returns calculated in dollar terms, rose 0.15 percent to 121.97 by the start of play on Friday.
By region, Latin America was up 0.38 percent to 98.98, Asia rose 0.13 to 128.90, and East Europe was up 0.04 at 159.64. --Caroline Brothers, London Newsroom +44 171 542 2734
